percentage.purpose: The utilisation number beside each meter. The only element on the page allowed above 1.5rem.

readout.purpose: The four aggregate totals: input, output, cache read, cost.

heading.purpose: Every h2. Sentence case, sans, at reading size.

body.purpose: Status text, notices, and the first-run message.

label.purpose: Window names, reset times, notes, buttons, the live lamp.

caption.purpose: Chart axis, origin chips, table headers, totals labels, the unit under a percentage.

figure.purpose: Table cells and measured values embedded in prose. Always tabular.

motion.name: meter-fill
motion.purpose: The only motion rule on the page. Covers the first paint and every subsequent poll with one declaration.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: The transition is removed entirely, not shortened.

contrast.floor: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and non-text indicators
contrast.measured: Audited in-browser against each element's rendered backdrop. Zero failures; the lowest ratio on the page is 4.61:1 on text-mute.
contrast.purpose: This page is read at about two metres, so contrast is a functional requirement rather than a compliance one.

components.name: Meter
components.description: The limit meter. A filled track read by length, with the percentage to its left and its unit beneath. Quarter notches sit above the fill so the bar can be read without the numeral. Fill colour is the status; a derived reading takes the neutral fill at every value.
components.html: 42%used
components.css: .ds-window-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; } .ds-value { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-end; min-width: 4.2ch; } .ds-percent { font-family: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 3.25rem); font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; letter-spacing: -.03em; line-height: 1; color: #e8ebef; } .ds-percent span { font-size: .4em; color: #78828f; } .ds-unit { margin-top: 5px; font-size: .75rem; color: #78828f; } .ds-meter { position: relative; flex: 1; height: 12px; border-radius: 4px; background: #1b1f26; overflow: hidden; } .ds-meter::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0; background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0 calc(25% - 1px), rgb(0 0 0 / .45) calc(25% - 1px), rgb(0 0 0 / .45) 25%); } .ds-fill { height: 100%; border-radius: inherit; background: #3ecf8e; transition: width .4s ease; }

components.name: Daily Chart
components.description: Daily history as one bar per day, height proportional to that day's tokens against the range peak. Idle days keep a 2% stub so a quiet week reads as quiet days rather than as a gap. The axis carries the first date, the peak value and the last date.
components.html: 14 Julpeak 853M tokens8 Aug
components.css: .ds-bars { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; gap: 2px; height: 110px; } .ds-bars div { flex: 1; min-width: 2px; border-radius: 2px 2px 0 0; background: #a3acb9; } .ds-bars .ds-idle { background: #333a45; } .ds-axis { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; margin-top: 8px; padding-top: 8px; border-top: 1px solid #262b33; font-family: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: .75rem; color: #78828f; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The primary container. One surface step above the ground with a hairline edge and no shadow. The header carries the name and the origin chip.
components.css: .ds-card { padding: 20px; border: 1px solid #262b33; border-radius: 6px; background: #14171c; color: #e8ebef; } .ds-card-head { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; } .ds-h2 { margin: 0; font-family: "IBM Plex Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: .875rem; font-weight: 600; color: #e8ebef; } .ds-chip { padding: 3px 8px; border: 1px solid #262b33; border-radius: 4px; font-size: .75rem; color: #78828f; } .ds-chip-live { border-color: #4d9fff; color: #4d9fff; }

components.name: Top Bar
components.description: A plain header. The wordmark is set at body size because a masthead would spend the top of the viewport that the limits need; the timezone and the live switch sit at the right.
components.css: .ds-topbar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; padding: 12px 24px; border-bottom: 1px solid #262b33; background: #14171c; font-family: "IBM Plex Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: .9375rem; color: #e8ebef; } .ds-mark { font-weight: 600; } .ds-zone { margin-left: auto; font-family: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: .8125rem; color: #78828f; }

components.name: Range Button
components.description: The only navigation on the surface. Ghost at rest; the active one takes a surface fill and a stronger edge rather than the accent, so selection does not compete with the live switch.
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; gap: 4px; } .ds-btn { border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 4px; padding: 4px 10px; background: transparent; color: #78828f; font-family: "IBM Plex Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: .8125rem; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn:hover { background: #1b1f26; color: #e8ebef; } .ds-btn.ds-active { border-color: #333a45; background: #1b1f26; color: #e8ebef; } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #4d9fff; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Live Lamp
components.description: The live-readings switch. The native input is visually hidden and every state is carried by :has() on the label. It is built once and updated in place, never remounted, because remounting takes keyboard focus with it.
components.css: .ds-lamp { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 5px 10px 5px 9px; border: 1px solid #262b33; border-radius: 4px; background: #1b1f26; color: #a3acb9; font-family: "IBM Plex Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: .8125rem; cursor: pointer; } .ds-lamp::before { content: ""; width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: #78828f; } .ds-lamp input { position: absolute; opacity: 0; width: 0; height: 0; } .ds-lamp:has(input:checked) { border-color: #4d9fff; color: #e8ebef; } .ds-lamp:has(input:checked)::before { background: #4d9fff; } .ds-lamp:has(input:focus-visible) { outline: 2px solid #4d9fff; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-lamp:has(input:disabled) { opacity: .55; cursor: progress; }

components.name: Origin Chip
components.description: A one-word statement of where a reading came from: live, stale, uncalibrated, or no reading. Tinted border and text, never a filled background, and provenance is never signalled by colour alone.
components.css: .ds-chip { padding: 3px 8px; border: 1px solid #262b33; border-radius: 4px; font-family: "IBM Plex Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: .75rem; color: #78828f; } .ds-chip-live { border-color: #4d9fff; color: #4d9fff; } .ds-chip-stale { border-color: #f5a524; color: #f5a524; }

components.name: Readout Row
components.description: Four aggregate totals seamed with 1px gaps that show the border colour through. Folds to 2x2 below 900px and stacks below 480px.
components.css: .ds-readouts { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); gap: 1px; margin: 0; padding: 0; border: 1px solid #262b33; border-radius: 6px; background: #262b33; overflow: hidden; } .ds-readouts div { padding: 16px; background: #14171c; } .ds-readouts dt { font-family: "IBM Plex Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: .75rem; color: #78828f; } .ds-readouts dd { margin: 6px 0 0; font-family: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 1.375rem; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #e8ebef; }

components.name: Notice
components.description: The system admitting a gap in its own data — unpriced models, a live-switch error. A warn rule on a plain surface rather than a filled panel, so it informs without alarming.
components.html: Cost excludes unpriced models: cohere/north-mini-code:free, and 2 more
components.css: .ds-notice { margin: 0; padding: 11px 14px; border: 1px solid #262b33; border-left: 3px solid #f5a524; border-radius: 4px; background: #14171c; color: #a3acb9; font-family: "IBM Plex Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: .875rem; }

narrative.overview:
This surface has one job and a fixed viewing distance. It runs on a second monitor in a room lit by other screens, is left open for hours, and is glanced at while both hands are busy elsewhere. It must answer how much headroom is left, and when it comes back, without being touched, clicked, or leaned toward.

Every decision is downstream of that distance. The interface is deliberately plain: neutral dark surfaces, one step of elevation, hairlines instead of shadow, sentence-case labels at readable sizes, and exactly one large element per meter. Nothing is styled to be noticed; things are styled to be read.

This replaced a metaphor-driven system (a darkroom under safelight) that encoded the limit as a ten-patch tonal step wedge and the history as cell lightness. Both were internally coherent and both failed the distance test — a value you have to decode is not a value you can glance at. Meters now read by length and history by height, which are the channels people judge most accurately at range.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral near-black ground; a single surface step; hairline borders; no shadows.
One accent for interaction, three status colours for state, no decorative colour at all.
The limits open the page at full width; history, cost and tables sit below as reference.
Meters read by length, history by height.
Mono with tabular numerals for every number; sans in sentence case for everything else.
One motion rule on the whole page.

rules.name: The Accent Is Not A State
rules.body: Blue means you can operate this — the live switch, the live chip, focus rings. If a new element wants to say something is wrong, nearly full, or fine, it uses the status scale. If it wants attention for its own sake, it gets a neutral.

rules.name: The Provenance Rule
rules.body: Status colour belongs to measured readings only. A derived estimate is measured against the busiest window in local history, so it reaches 100% the moment the current window is the busiest one recorded — an artefact of a thin baseline, not a limit being reached. A derived meter stays text-mute at every value and labels itself uncalibrated. This is a product constraint from PRODUCT.md before it is a visual one, and it is enforced in meterState() in web/app.js.

rules.name: No Shadows
rules.body: Depth is the ground/surface step plus a hairline. Shadow blurs at the viewing distance this page is designed for and buys nothing at any other.

rules.name: One Large Thing
rules.body: The meter percentage is the only element allowed above 1.5rem. It is what resolves first from across the room; if a second element competed, neither would.

rules.name: Mono Is Measurement
rules.body: Every percentage, token count, cost, reset time and table figure is set in Plex Mono with tabular-nums, so a figure that changes on a poll does not reflow the row it sits in. Sans is for sentences.

rules.name: Every Track Is minmax(0, ...)
rules.body: A grid track sized auto refuses to shrink below its content, so one long model name is enough to push the whole document wider than the viewport. Tables scroll inside their own card instead.

rules.name: Limits Are The Page
rules.body: The first viewport is the top bar and the limit cards. Nothing — no wordmark block, no summary cards, no chart — may be inserted above them.

dos: Do put the number and the bar in the same row, and let the bar be the redundant one.
Do use the status scale for state and the accent for interaction.
Do set every figure in IBM Plex Mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.
Do say what a reading is when it is not measured — uncalibrated is information, not an excuse.
Do distinguish 'no block open' from 'no fixed reset'; they are different facts.
Do keep new grid tracks at minmax(0, ...) so content cannot widen the page.
Do give every focusable element the same 2px solid accent ring at 2px offset.
Do design for a two-metre glance first: if a new element cannot be read from across the room, it belongs below the fold.
donts: Don't add a fourth surface level, a shadow, or a gradient.
Don't spend the accent on anything that is not operable.
Don't set a label in uppercase with letterspacing.
Don't encode a quantity as lightness, saturation, or texture.
Don't add a second large element to the first viewport.
Don't fetch a font, script or stylesheet from a CDN — the three files are served verbatim from the Go binary's embedded filesystem, with no build step and no framework.
Don't exceed the four shipped font files (Sans 400/600, Mono 400/600), and don't use italics.
